rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation is in instance_norm_forward_kernel (non-affine). ModelNew uses InstanceNorm2dCustom with affine=True (default). CUDA dispatch: weight.defined() && bias.defined() → uses instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine (unmutated). The mutated kernel is never invoked.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation affects the non-affine variant of the instance normalization kernel (instance_norm_forward_kernel). However, the ModelNew class instantiates InstanceNorm2dCustom with the default affine=True parameter. When affine is true, nn.Parameter tensors are created for weight and bias, which are then passed to the CUDA function. The C++ dispatch logic checks 'weight.defined() && bias.defined()' and routes to instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine, which contains the original correct reduction code. The mutated kernel code path is architecturally unreachable under the fixed model configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed configuration. Would require changing affine=False in InstanceNorm2dCustom instantiation, which violates the testing contract that shapes and model configuration are fixed.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing GPU kernels with multiple code paths (e.g., affine vs non-affine variants), ensure mutations in each variant are tested with appropriate model configurations. Consider adding explicit test coverage flags or conditional compilation to verify all kernel variants are exercised.
